summary: Iran conducted multiple missile launches from Aligoodarz, Nurabad Mamasani, and Saqqez within hours, while Israel eliminated two Hamas internal security chiefs in Gaza City. Houthis struck Riyadh's Public Investment Fund tower for the second time in five days, injuring 11. Israeli forces intensified attacks across southern Lebanon with 143 alerts recorded on November 24.
key_points: Iran launched missiles from three provinces: Lorestan, Fars, and Kurdistan within a six-hour window. (Source: @shin_persian/12835, @shin_persian/12827, @shin_persian/12837)
Israel confirmed killing Hamas internal security chief Naim Abu Nahal in Gaza City strike. (Source: @manniefabian/59580)
Senior Hamas commander Muhammad Abu al-Awf killed with wife and two daughters in Shati camp strike. (Source: @manniefabian/59582)
Houthis attacked Riyadh's Public Investment Fund tower second time in five days, 11 injured. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10395)
Iran added 26 tugs to Strait of Hormuz Non-Compliance List, targeting maritime support vessels. (Source: @shin_persian/12838)
Israeli attacks across Lebanon November 24: 143 alerts, 75 drone sightings, artillery at 18 locations. (Source: @redlinkleb/54922)
Suicide drone exploded in car in Tulin, Lebanon, no casualties reported. (Source: @redlinkleb/54939)
Israeli Defense Minister Katz claims Iran developing chemical weapons, vows prevention. (Source: @manniefabian/59581)

sections.executive_summary: Iran conducted coordinated missile launches from Aligoodarz (Lorestan), Nurabad Mamasani (Fars), and Saqqez (Kurdistan) within hours, signaling heightened military readiness. Israel eliminated two Hamas internal security chiefs in Gaza City within 24 hours: Naim Abu Nahal and Muhammad Abu al-Awf, the latter killed with his wife and two teenage daughters in Shati camp. Houthis struck Riyadh's Public Investment Fund tower for the second time in five days, injuring 11 people, while Israeli forces recorded 143 alerts across southern Lebanon including artillery shelling at 18 locations.

points: Missile launched from Aligoodarz, Lorestan Province at 1747Z, detected by FromIran monitoring dashboard with 120-second delay. (Source: @shin_persian/12835)
Missile launch observed around Nurabad Mamasani mountains, Fars Province at 17:48 local time (1418Z), posted via FromIran delayed feed. (Source: @shin_persian/12827)
Two missiles launched from Saqqez, Kurdistan Province at 21:15 local time (1745Z), recorded by FromIran dashboard with standard delay. (Source: @shin_persian/12837)
Jet activity heard in Dezful, Khuzestan Province at 18:27 local time (1457Z), reported via FromIran delayed posting system. (Source: @shin_persian/12829)

Iran added 26 tugs and offshore support vessels to Strait of Hormuz Non-Compliance List for assisting ships using southern corridor without Iranian permission; three tugs attacked this year including MUSSAFAH 2 sunk in March. (Source: @shin_persian/12838)
Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz confirmed IDF struck and killed Hamas internal security chief Naim Abu Nahal in Gaza City. (Source: @manniefabian/59580)
Defense Minister Katz stated Iran is "in the process of developing chemical weapons" and declared Israel "will not allow Iran to attain a chemical weapon." (Source: @manniefabian/59581)
IDF strike on Shati camp killed Muhammad Abu al-Awf, 47, director of internal security in northern Gaza Strip, along with his wife and two teenage daughters. (Source: @manniefabian/59582)
Second Hamas internal security chief eliminated within 24 hours, following Naim Abu Nahal's killing the previous day. (Source: @manniefabian/59582)
Hamas internal security chief Naim Abu Nahal killed in Israeli strike in Gaza City, confirmed by both Israeli leadership and Hamas. (Source: @manniefabian/59580)
Senior Hamas commander Muhammad Abu al-Awf, 47, director of internal security for northern Gaza Strip, killed in overnight strike on Shati camp. (Source: @manniefabian/59582)
Strike on Shati camp also killed Abu al-Awf's wife and two teenage daughters, according to Hamas interior ministry. (Source: @manniefabian/59582)
Two consecutive days of targeted killings decapitated Hamas internal security leadership in Gaza City. (Source: @manniefabian/59580, @manniefabian/59582)

Daily statistics November 24: Israeli airstrikes hit Kfar Tibnit, Qabrikha, Tulin; artillery shelling at 18 locations including Hadata (5 rounds), Wadi al-Hajar (4), Wadi Zibqin (4), Zibqin (3), Barishit (3), Ali al-Tahir (2). (Source: @redlinkleb/54922)
Explosions recorded at Rab al-Thalathin (3), Al-Tiri, Kfar Tibnit; machine gun sweeping in Khiam (2), Hadata (2), Kfar Shuba, Shebaa, Bayt Yahoun. (Source: @redlinkleb/54922)
Drone sightings highest in Majdal Salm (6), Tulin (5), Al-Ghandouriya (5), Qabrikha (5), Dahieh (5); 143 total alerts, 75 drone detections. (Source: @redlinkleb/54922)
Suicide drone exploded in car in Tulin town with no casualties; new explosion in Aynata around 1:30 at same location as previous blast. (Source: @redlinkleb/54939, @redlinkleb/54937)

Large explosion by Israeli army in Al-Tiri town approximately 40 minutes before reporting; artillery shelling in Wadi al-Salouqi and Zoutr al-Sharqiya. (Source: @redlinkleb/54901, @redlinkleb/54919, @redlinkleb/54980)
No relevant conflict activity reported in Syria or Iraq from provided sources during this period.
Houthis struck Riyadh's Public Investment Fund tower for second time in five days, injuring 11 people according to Wall Street Journal reporting. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10395)
Iran's Strait of Hormuz Non-Compliance List expansion to 26 tugs and offshore vessels directly threatens Gulf maritime logistics and energy transit. (Source: @shin_persian/12838)

key_developments: Iran launched missiles from three separate locations — Aligoodarz (Lorestan), Nurabad Mamasani (Fars), Saqqez (Kurdistan) — between 1418Z and 1747Z, indicating coordinated readiness. (Source: @shin_persian/12835, @shin_persian/12827, @shin_persian/12837)

Israel eliminated two Hamas internal security chiefs in Gaza City within 24 hours: Naim Abu Nahal and Muhammad Abu al-Awf (with family) in Shati camp strike. (Source: @manniefabian/59580, @manniefabian/59582)
Houthis conducted second attack on Riyadh's Public Investment Fund tower in five days, causing 11 injuries, demonstrating persistent long-range capability. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10395)

Iran designated 26 tugs and offshore vessels to Strait of Hormuz Non-Compliance List, escalating maritime pressure after three tug attacks this year including MUSSAFAH 2 sinking. (Source: @shin_persian/12838)
Israeli forces generated 143 alerts across southern Lebanon November 24, with 75 drone sightings, artillery at 18 locations, and airstrikes on three villages. (Source: @redlinkleb/54922)
Suicide drone attack on vehicle in Tulin, Lebanon caused no casualties; simultaneous explosion in Aynata at previously targeted site. (Source: @redlinkleb/54939, @redlinkleb/54937)
Israeli Defense Minister Katz publicly accused Iran of developing chemical weapons and vowed to prevent acquisition, raising threshold for potential preemptive action. (Source: @manniefabian/59581)
sections.threat_assessment: Iran's simultaneous missile launches from three provinces suggest either a coordinated exercise or heightened alert posture, possibly linked to Israeli strikes in Gaza and Lebanon. The elimination of Hamas's entire internal security leadership in 24 hours creates a command vacuum that may degrade internal control but could trigger retaliatory attacks. Houthi repetition against Riyadh's financial district indicates improved targeting persistence. Iran's maritime non-compliance list expansion threatens commercial shipping support infrastructure, raising insurance costs and delaying emergency response in the Strait of Hormuz.
sections.regional_response: Israeli leadership publicly confirmed strikes on Hamas security chiefs while Defense Minister Katz escalated rhetoric on Iranian chemical weapons, signaling a dual-track approach of kinetic action and strategic deterrence. Lebanese monitoring channels document daily Israeli attack patterns but lack intercept or response capabilities. Gulf states face compounding threats: Houthi missile reach into Riyadh and Iranian pressure on maritime logistics. No coordinated regional defense posture is evident from available sources.
sections.intelligence_notes: FromIran's 120-second delayed missile launch reporting provides near-real-time Iranian missile tracking but may miss mobile launcher relocation. Lebanese Red Alert's granular daily statistics (round counts per village, drone sightings per location) offer high-resolution battle damage assessment potential. Houthi targeting of the same Riyadh tower twice in five days suggests either battle damage assessment confirmation or symbolic persistence. Iranian tug designation list includes specific IMO numbers per source, enabling precise vessel tracking.
